info.title: Atmospheric Model
info.description:
This API allows you to retrieve orders for Atmospheric Model Data otherwise 
    known as ‘Gridded’ data. The API described here contains a definition for all 
    requests as well as examples of how to write your code to interface with our 
    gateway to retrieve your data.

 When you call this API you will need your API key and
    can begin by making a call to /1.0.0/orders (this will give you all of your
    Order IDs).

 API Usage is typically done in 4 Steps

 1. Call GET /1.0.0/orders - to programmatically get each order's "orderId"
    field

 2. Call GET /1.0.0/orders/{orderId}/latest - to get a list of "fileId"
    entries (these represent all the files available for this order)

 3. Call GET /1.0.0/orders/{orderId}/latest/{fileId} - to get more detailed
    information about each file if required

 4. Call GET /1.0.0/orders/{orderId}/latest/{fileId}/data - with an Accept
    header of application/x-grib to get access to a specific GRIB file

 There are additional end points to query the runs available:

 1. Call GET /1.0.0/runs - to get each available run

 2. Call GET /1.0.0/runs/{modelId} - to get each available run for a
    particular model

 Using your application, you can go through multiple
    orders and then retrieve the files for each.

 Please be aware that the files could be delivered by redirecting your
    client, so your client should follow any HTTP 302 redirects it gets to allow
    it to download the file. Please note the file ID will need to be URL encoded.

 This is done in Curl by adding -L or --location (in programming languages,
    you will need to visit the new URL to get your file).

 If there are any errors or issues, each endpoint will provide an appropriate
    HTTP response and may provide a JSON body providing you with further helpful
    information, so please do not forget to check for errors.

 If you are testing before development or downloading using scripts with a
    tool like Curl you can view errors using --verbose. If you do not do this it
    could just appear that you are getting "nothing back".

get.summary: Provide a list of the latest available data files for the specified order.
get.description: Provide a list of available files for the order created in the Atmospheric Weather Data Tool. This contains metadata such as fileId, the runs, the region selected and the parameters and time steps selected.

parameters.name: orderId
parameters.description: The order ID that you wish to retrieve information for. This could be different to your order name as entered on the Atmospheric Weather Data Tool because certain characters are removed from that name. Please ensure you check for the API Order ID on the Order Summary page or use the one retrieved from a call to /orders.

parameters.name: detail
parameters.description: Optional level of detail in the response. Valid options are MINIMAL or FULL. Default is FULL.

parameters.name: runfilter
parameters.description: Optional filter to limit listed files. Valid options are CURRENT for latest run, YYYYMMDDRR or RR. Where RR is the run hour.

parameters.name: dataSpec
parameters.description: The data specification to use, only version 1.1.0 is currently supported.

get.summary: Provide the details of a specific file that can be obtained for the latest available data.
get.description: Provides metadata about a specific fileId. For example you can find out what the file will contain including the surface identifier, the region it covers, the model generation time (run time) and the parameters, time steps and level information it contains.

get.summary: Gets the actual data for a specific file that can be obtained for the latest available data.
get.description: This endpoint provides the binary file data for a given file ID. Please note that the data will be returned from an alternative URL instead of directly. This means you will need to process an HTTP 302 and visit the URL given in the Location header to get the binary data stream containing the file contents.

parameters.name: orderId
parameters.description: The order ID that you wish to retrieve files for. The Order ID can be seen under a specific order on the Atmospheric Weather Data Tool Order Summary Page or found in the list of orders in the JSON response from your call to /1.0.0/orders

parameters.name: fileId
parameters.description: The file ID of the application/x-grib file you wish to retrieve information about. The file IDs can be seen on the Atmospheric Weather Data Tool Order Summary Page or found in the JSON response from your call to /1.0.0/orders/{orderId}/latest. Please note the file IDs will need to be URL encoded.

parameters.name: dataSpec
parameters.description: The data specification to use, only version 1.1.0 is currently supported.

parameters.name: Accept
parameters.description: application/x-grib required here to receive the 302. Once the  new location is visited the binary contents of the file will be made  available to your application.

302.description: HTTP redirect with a Location header that gives you the URL to visit to retrieve your file. Please ensure your application  can successfully handle redirects. If you are using a or similar  then please remember to pass the or location arguments to the  command to force it to follow the redirect and get the file content  on your behalf.
